title: Opportunistic Prefill Orchestrator: acceptance gauge, kernel-aware routing, and deferred fallthrough plan
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary: Implement an opportunistic prefill orchestrator that (1) probes candidate model variants with micro-prefill probes, (2) computes a lightweight acceptance_gauge per-request to decide whether to commit speculative decode output, and (3) routes requests to kernel-appropriate model variants with a deferred fallthrough strategy when acceptance is low or SLOs are at risk. This ticket covers design + prototype scheduler + simulation + canary rollout plan.

Motivation: Current speculative decode plumbing focuses on acceptance signals emitted mid-decode but doesn't account for kernel-level cost/latency differences and KV cache warmup patterns. We observe cases where a small probe on a quantized low-cost model would have been accepted but was never attempted due to static routing; conversely, some expensive fast-path kernels are selected but then stall due to kernel memory pressure. The orchestrator should increase overall throughput and lower median P95 latency regressions by being kernel-aware and accepting partial outputs only when acceptance_gauge indicates high confidence.

Acceptance gauge definition (proposal): a per-prefill scalar between 0.0-1.0 computed from:  - early-token perplexity delta (normalized)  - top-k token agreement with light-weight guess model (k=3)  - latency headroom margin relative to request SLO  - model-kernel match score (favors kernels that avoid memory thrashing)  We propose a linear-weighted score: acceptance = 0.45*perplexity_delta_score + 0.25*agreement_score + 0.2*latency_headroom + 0.1*kernel_match. Thresholds: accept if >= 0.85, soft-commit if in [0.65,0.85), defer and continue main decode if in [0.4,0.65), and force immediate fallback if <0.4 or if queueing delay > fallback_latency_threshold.

Kernel-aware routing heuristics:  - Prefer fused QKV / flash-attention kernels for seq_len > 1024 when memory headroom exists.  - Prefer quantized int8 kernels on smaller GPUs (A10/A16) when model quantization impact on acceptance is small.  - ModelVariantScore = alpha*estimated_cycles + beta*mem_pressure_penalty + gamma*expected_kv_warmup_gain.  - Use a fast fingerprint to select kernel family at admission time; adjust routing if observed kernel latency deviates >20% from estimate.

Prefill and scheduling:  - Micro-prefill probes (1-3 tokens) are dispatched as high-priority, low-batch micro-requests to candidate model variants to warm KV caches and produce acceptance signals.  - Probes use a short TTL for their KV entries (configurable, default 30s) and are eligible for reuse across requests from the same tenant for similar prompt prefixes.  - Scheduler groups probes by kernel affinity to enable contiguous kernel runs and reduce kernel startup/teardown overhead.  - Backpressure: maintain separate probe queues with SLO-aware prioritization; if probe queue length threatens 95th latency SLO for main decodes, suspend probes and route to fallback deterministically.

Fallback policy (deferred fallthrough):  - If acceptance gauge fails or kernel mismatch occurs, we first attempt an async fast-fallback to a lower-cost variant that previously had >=0.8 acceptance for similar inputs.  - If async fallback still misses acceptance, perform synchronous conservative decode on baseline model (pinned heavy variant) to ensure correctness.  - Emit diagnostics events: fallback_reason, chosen_fallback_variant, probe_latency, and acceptance_trace for postmortem analysis.

Telemetry / Metrics:  - acceptance_rate, acceptance_by_variant, probe_success_rate, probe_latency_ms_p50/p95, fallback_rate, kernel_mismatch_rate, kv_cache_reuse_rate.  - Correlate acceptance with downstream quality metrics (chat turn BLEU/ROUGE proxy, SDK-level user-visible latency).  - Add synthetic workload simulation to generate expected distributions and validate thresholds before canary.

Deliverables / Milestones: 1) Design doc + simulation harness (this ticket) 2) Prototype scheduler & probe dispatcher (unit tests + perf harness) 3) Telemetry pipeline + dashboard (dev cluster) 4) Canary (10% traffic, runtime-1.22) 5) Rollout with gradual increase and rollback playbook.

Risks & trade-offs:  - Probes add overhead; must be strictly SLO-aware and throttleable.  - Acceptance gauge false positives risk returning lower-quality outputs; mitigate with conservative thresholds and quick rollback.  - Kernel heuristics complexity increases routing path; keep model of kernel costs small and empirical.

Open questions:  - What are the final weights for acceptance components? (need ablation in sim)  - How long to retain probe KV entries across tenants/requests? (privacy/OSS trade-offs)  - Do we expose opt-out to customers at API level or keep entirely platform-side?
